Hi Karthik / Priyom,

We're seeing a significant p95/p99 regression across multiple endpoints in our production environment starting ~07:50 PT. Impact: order ingestion timeouts and consumer retries. Error samples attached (fintechco-error-snapshot-0706.txt).

Symptoms observed: 
- P95 up from ~120ms to ~2.1s, P99 spiking to 9–12s
- Elevated 429 rate (up 14x) and a correlating rise in client-side retries that appear to be compounding latency
- Several timed-out requests surfaced in our worker queues, leading to duplicated downstream work

We need an immediate mitigation plan — this is affecting several customers. Can you confirm receipt and advise short-term steps (disable retries, throttle, or whitelist)? We're also happy to join a war room.

Preliminary findings from logs and the serving dashboard (see link):  https://console.redwood.ai/dashboard/fintechco/requests?range=1h  (PD-8921).

What we see:
- A small subset (~0.6% of client keys belonging to FintechCo) emitted large bursts starting 07:48 PT. Those bursts coincide with repeated client retries with near-zero backoff.
- Our rate limiter (per-customer token-bucket) is hitting the burst window frequently; when limiter rejects we return 429. Clients retry immediately, which increases incoming QPS and pushes more requests into the tail — classic retry amplification.
- The serving pools are saturated on a few nodes handling long sequences; this raises tail latency and causes internal timeouts, which feed 429s upstream.

Short-term mitigations we can apply in the next 15–30m (no code deploy required):
1) Switch FintechCo to a conservative policy: reduce their burst allowance and enable server-side Retry-After header (will instruct client to back off).
2) Temporarily enable jittered exponential backoff enforcement via response headers + reduce client retry default in our SDKs (config override for FintechCo).
3) Move FintechCo traffic to an isolated burst pool (create a temporary shard) to protect other customers. This requires capacity allocation; if we need to spin up new nodes, that will take ~20–40m.

I've attached a quick p95 report (p95-report-0706.csv) and a short analysis showing correlation between 429 spikes and retry loops.

I'll lead the triage — Rishi, can you validate whether we can reconfigure the token bucket parameters and spin up the temporary shard without breaking other SLAs?

— Marissa
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API latency & 429s - production impact

Quick update after in-depth check (logs + runtime telemetry):
- Cause: Retry amplification due to aggressive client retry loops + conservative token-bucket burst settings. The interplay created a positive feedback loop — 429 -> immediate retry -> queue growth -> tail timeouts -> more 429s.
- Mitigations applied (09:00 PT):
  * Temporarily increased FintechCo's burst quota by 2x on a small isolated shard (moved ~15% of their traffic). This reduced immediate 429s for that shard.
  * Enabled Retry-After header with a 6s suggested backoff for 429 responses.
  * Applied jittered backoff guidance via header and pushed an SDK config override to FintechCo (they confirmed it was accepted).

Observed effect: p95 fell from ~2.1s to ~600ms within 8–10 minutes for the isolated shard, overall P99 reduced but still elevated on some long-sequence nodes.

Recommended next steps (need approvals):
A) Keep the isolated shard live for 24–48h while we tune token-bucket parameters and deploy a more robust request-shedder. This consumes reserved capacity; commercial approval required for emergency capacity allocation.
B) For broader platform hardening: expose server-side Retry-After + X-RateLimit-Reset headers on all 429s and default the hosted SDKs to a safer retry policy (rollout over 2 weeks).

Attachments: throttle-analysis-0706.csv (correlation & node-level stats).

Priyom / Karthik: for A) we need a short-term commercial OK to allocate capacity and consider a one-time credit to FintechCo for the duplicated work they observed. Vivek — looking for quick sign-off to proceed.

— Rishi
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

- Immediate work done: temporary isolated shard spun up, Retry-After header enabled, SDK override pushed. Early results positive (p95 dropping).
